en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Heart of Great Compassion, Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed, of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes,
translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta from Western India during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, Śākyamuni Buddha was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, within the palace of Avalokiteśvara, in the midst of the jewel-adorned site of enlightenment, seated upon a precious lion throne.
That seat was purely adorned with immeasurable varieties of *maṇi* jewels, with banners and streamers made of a hundred precious gems suspended and arranged all around it.
At that time, the Tathāgata, upon that seat, was about to expound the *dhāraṇī* of universal retention (*saṃgraha-dhāraṇī*).
He was accompanied by countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were:

Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīrāja, Bodhisattva Ratnarāja, Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Bodhisattva Avataṃsaka, Bodhisattva Mahāvyūha, Bodhisattva Ratnagarbha, Bodhisattva Guṇagarbha, Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, Bodhisattva Maitreya, Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, and Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. These and other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were all great Dharma-princes who had received the consecration.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable and innumerable great śrāvaka monks, all of whom had practiced the ten stages of arhatship, with Mahākāśyapa as their leader.
He was also accompanied by immeasurable Brahmakāyika devas, with Sunakṣatra Brahmā as their leader.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable devaputras of the desire realm, with the devaputra Gopaka as their leader.
He was also accompanied by immeasurable World-Protecting Four Kings, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra as their leader.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, with the Great Nāga King Devaśrī as their leader.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable goddesses of the desire realm, with the goddess Tārakākṣī as their leader.

Also present were immeasurable deities of space, deities of rivers and seas, deities of springs and sources, deities of streams and ponds, deities of medicinal herbs, deities of forests, deities of dwellings, deities of water, deities of fire, deities of earth, deities of wind, deities of soil, deities of mountains, deities of rocks, and deities of palaces; all had come to assemble there.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara secretly manifested supernatural powers within the great assembly; his radiance shone forth, so that the lands of the ten directions as well as this trichiliocosm were all turned the color of gold.
The palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, and the palaces of all the honored deities all shook;
the rivers, the great oceans, the Cakravāḍa mountains, Mount Sumeru, the earthen hills, and the Black Mountains likewise trembled violently.
The light of the sun, moon, jewels, fire, and the constellations all ceased to appear.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīrāja, beholding this rare phenomenon, marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
He immediately rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and questioned the Buddha in verse regarding these signs of supernatural power: "By whom were these released?
Who has today attained perfect enlightenment? He asked in verse: "Who has today realized true awakening?"
Universally emitting such great radiance, the lands of the ten directions all become golden, and the trichiliocosm is likewise so.
Who has attained mastery this day?
He manifests and releases rare and great supernormal powers, causing all boundless Buddha-lands to tremble; the palaces of the nāgas and devas are all unsettled.
Now this great assembly is filled with doubt, unable to fathom the causes and conditions—whose power is this?
Are you a Buddha, a Bodhisattva, or a great Śrāvaka?
Are you a Brahmā, a Māra, a Deva, or one of the Śakras?
We pray only that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion, will explain the origin of these supernormal powers!
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīrāja, saying: "Good son!
You should know that within this assembly there is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara."

Having accomplished great kindness and great compassion since immeasurable kalpas past, and being well-able to cultivate immeasurable dharani-gates, he has secretly manifested such great supernormal powers for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
When the Buddha had spoken these words,
at that time the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One!"
I possess the Great Compassion Heart Dhāraṇī mantra, which I now wish to proclaim.

It is for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings; for the purpose of eliminating all illnesses; for the attainment of longevity; for the attainment of abundance; for the eradication of all evil karma and grave offenses; for liberation from obstacles and hardships; for the increase of all pure dharmas and merits; for the fulfillment of all roots of goodness; for the distancing of all fears; and for the swift satisfaction of all aspirations.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion and pity, will grant me permission!
The Buddha said,
"Good son!..."
"You possess great compassion and bring peace and happiness to sentient beings.
You wish to proclaim a divine mantra; now is the very time to do so, and you should speak it swiftly.
The Tathāgata rejoices in this, and all Buddhas do likewise."
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I recall that in the past, immeasurable billions of kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named 'Tathāgata Tranquil Abiding of the King of a Thousand Lights. "
Out of compassion for me and for the sake of all sentient beings, that Buddha, the World-Honored One, has preached this "Dhāraṇī of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassionate Heart."
With his golden hand, he stroked the crown of my head and spoke these words: "Good son!
You should uphold this heart-mantra and universally bring great benefit and happiness to all sentient beings in the evil world of the future."
"At that time, I was just established in the first stage (*bhūmi*); yet by hearing this dhāraṇī once, I transcended to the eighth stage.
Because my heart was filled with joy, I immediately made this vow:
'If, in the future, I am able to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, may my body instantly be endowed with a thousand hands and a thousand eyes.'"
“Having made this vow, at that very moment, my body was fully endowed with a thousand hands and a thousand eyes;
the great earth of the ten directions shook in six ways;
and the thousand Buddhas of the ten directions all emitted radiance, which touched my body and illuminated the boundless worlds of the ten directions.”
"From that time forward, in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas and within immeasurable assemblies, he again heard this dhāraṇī, receiving it personally and upholding it."
He again gave rise to joy, leaping for immeasurable delight, and immediately transcended the subtle cycle of birth and death across countless billions of kalpas.

From that time forth, he has constantly recited and upheld this mantra without ever forgetting it; by virtue of upholding this dhāraṇī, wherever he is born, he always appears before the Buddha, born miraculously from a lotus flower, never receiving a body born from a womb.

"If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, boys, or girls who wish to recite and uphold [this], they should first arouse a heart of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings and follow me by making this vow:
'Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!'"
May I swiftly come to know all dharmas.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I soon attain the eye of wisdom.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I swiftly deliver all sentient beings.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I quickly attain skillful means.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I swiftly board the ship of Prajñā.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I swiftly cross the ocean of suffering.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I swiftly attain the path of precepts and meditative concentration!
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I soon ascend the mountain of Nirvāṇa!
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I swiftly reach the abode of the unconditioned.
Homage to the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara!
May I soon become one with the Dharmatā-body.
“If I head toward the Mountain of Blades, the Mountain of Blades shall crumble of its own accord.
If I head toward the Cauldron of Fire, the Cauldron of Fire shall extinguish of its own accord.”
If I am headed for hell, hell itself shall dry up;
If I am headed for the realm of hungry ghosts, the hungry ghosts shall be spontaneously satiated;
If I am headed for the asuras, their evil minds shall be naturally subdued.
"If I am reborn among the animals, may I spontaneously attain great wisdom.

Having made this vow, one should sincerely invoke my name and also single-mindedly recollect my original teacher, Amitābha Tathāgata; thereafter, one should immediately chant this divine dhāraṇī mantra.
"If one recites it five times in a single night, the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas within one's body shall be extinguished.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
If there are humans or devas who recite and uphold these phrases of Great Compassion, when their life comes to an end, the Buddhas of the ten directions will all come to extend their hands to them.
Whatever Buddha-land they wish to be born in, they shall attain rebirth there in accordance with their vow.
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If any sentient beings who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra should fall into the three evil realms, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment."
"If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassion Dhāraṇī do not attain birth in the lands of all Buddhas, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassion Dhāraṇī do not obtain immeasurable samādhis and eloquence, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment."

"If those who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra do not have all their requests fulfilled within their present lifetime, it cannot be considered the Great Compassionate Heart Dharani."
"Except for those who commit unwholesome deeds and those who lack sincerity.
If there are women who loathe and despise their female bodies and desire to attain a male body, they should recite and uphold the chapters and phrases of the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī."
If I do not transform this female body into a male body, I vow not to attain perfect enlightenment.
Should anyone harbor even a slight doubt, their aspiration shall certainly not be fulfilled.

"If there are sentient beings who plunder or damage the permanent endowments, food, or wealth of the Sangha, even if a thousand Buddhas appear in the world, they will not be permitted to repent; even if they do repent, their transgressions shall not be extinguished."
If one now recites the Great Compassion Dhāraṇī, it shall be immediately extinguished.

However, if one has encroached upon or consumed the food, drink, or property belonging to the Sangha, one must first offer repentance and apology before the teachers of the ten directions; only then will it be extinguished.
Now, when one recites the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī, the teachers of the ten directions immediately arrive to act as witnesses; all karmic obstacles and hindrances are completely extinguished.

All ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, slandering people, slandering the Dharma, breaking the fast, violating the precepts, destroying stupas, ruining monasteries, stealing the property of the Sangha, and defiling pure celibacy—all such evil karmas and grave offenses shall be completely extinguished.
With one exception: for those who harbor doubts regarding this mantra, even minor offenses and light karmic actions will not be extinguished, let alone grave sins.
Although it does not immediately extinguish grave sins, it can still serve as a remote cause for bodhi.
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If there are humans or devas who recite and uphold this Great Compassionate Heart Mantra, they shall obtain fifteen kinds of auspicious births and shall not undergo fifteen kinds of inauspicious deaths."
As for those who die a miserable death:
first, not to let them die from hunger, starvation, or suffering;
second, not to cause them to die through shackling, imprisonment, flogging, or corporal punishment.
Third, one does not die at the hands of enemies or adversaries.
Fourth, one does not die killed in the midst of military arrays.
Fifth, one does not die harmed by beasts of prey such as jackals or wolves.
Sixth, they shall not die from being stung by venomous snakes, vipers, or scorpions.
Seventh, they shall not die from being burned or swept away by water or fire.
Eighth, they shall not die from being poisoned by toxic drugs.
Ninth, they shall not die from the harm of bewitching poisons.
Tenth, they shall not die from madness or loss of mindfulness.
Eleventh, they shall not die from falling from mountains, trees, cliffs, or precipices.
Twelfth, one shall not die from being bewitched by wicked people.
Thirteenth, one shall not die at the hands of malevolent spirits or evil ghosts who find an opportunity to harm.
Fourteenth, one shall not die with a malignant illness ensnaring the body.
Fifteenth, one does not die through self-inflicted harm that is contrary to reason.
Those who recite and uphold this Great Compassion Divine Mantra shall not suffer these fifteen kinds of evil deaths.
"One who attains the fifteen kinds of noble births is as follows:
first, wherever they are born, they always encounter a virtuous king;
second, they are always born in a virtuous land."
Third, they always encounter auspicious times.
Fourth, they always meet with virtuous friends.
Fifth, their physical faculties are always fully intact.
Sixth, the mind of the Way is pure and mature.
Seventh, one does not transgress the prohibitive precepts.
Eighth, all one's kinsmen and followers are harmonious and compliant through kindness and righteousness.
Ninth, one’s necessities, wealth, and food will always be abundant and sufficient.
Tenth, one will constantly receive the respect and assistance of others.
Eleventh, one’s possessions and treasures will not be plundered by others.
Twelfth, whatever one seeks through the mind’s desires shall all be fulfilled accordingly.
Thirteenth, dragon deities and benevolent spirits will constantly provide protection and guardianship.
Fourteenth, in every place where one is born, one shall behold the Buddhas and hear the Dharma.
Fifteenth, one shall hear the true Dharma and awaken to its profound meaning.
Those who recite and uphold the Mahākaruṇā Dhāraṇī shall attain these fifteen kinds of virtuous births.
"All devas and humans should constantly recite and uphold this; do not give rise to indolence.

After the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken these words, he stood before the assembled multitude with palms joined, giving rise to a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings. With a face brightened by a gentle smile, he then spoke this "Great Dhāraṇī of the Heart of Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassion," the "Divine and Wondrous Chapter-Dhāraṇī," saying:

After the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had spoken this mantra, he said:
The great earth shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down precious flowers that fell in profusion.

All the Buddhas of the ten directions were filled with joy, while the heavenly Māras and non-Buddhists were struck with terror, their hair standing on end. The entire assembly attained the realization of the fruits of enlightenment.

Some attain the fruit of *srotāpanna*, some attain the fruit of *sakṛdāgāmin*, some attain the fruit of *anāgāmin*, and some attain the fruit of *arhat*; some attain the first bhūmi, the second bhūmi, the third bhūmi, the fourth bhūmi, the fifth bhūmi, and so on up to the tenth bhūmi.
Immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon Bodhi.
At that time, the Great Brahma Heaven King rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent!
"O Great Being!

Since the distant past, I have attended the assemblies of immeasurable Buddhas and have heard various teachings and various dhāraṇīs; yet I have never before heard such an exposition of this unimpeded great compassionate heart and these wondrous phrases of the Great Compassion Dhāraṇī."
"I only pray that the Great Being will explain for us the form, appearance, and characteristics of this dhāraṇī; we, the great assembly, wish and desire to hear it!
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Brahmā King, saying:
"It is because you act as a skillful means to benefit all sentient beings that you have asked such a question."
"Listen well now; I shall briefly explain it for you all!
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva said: "It is the mind of great compassion;

it is the mind of equanimity; it is the unconditioned mind; it is the mind free from attachment; it is the mind of the contemplation of emptiness; it is the mind of reverence; it is the humble mind; it is the mind free from confusion and distraction; it is the mind free from dogmatic views; it is the unsurpassed mind of Bodhi."
"You should know that such states of mind as these are the characteristics of dhāraṇī.
You should practice in accordance with this.
The Great Brahmā King said:
"We, the great assembly, have now for the first time recognized the characteristics of this dhāraṇī.
From this day forward, we shall uphold it and dare not forget it.
Avalokiteśvara said:
"If any good man or good woman recites and upholds this divine mantra, they shall give rise to the vast bodhicitta and vow to deliver all sentient beings."
Maintain the fast and precepts, and give rise to a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.
Constantly recite this mantra without interruption.
Dwell in a pure chamber, bathe until you are clean, and wear clean clothing.
Hang up banners, light lamps, offer incense, flowers, and food of a hundred flavors as offerings.
Concentrate the mind on a single point without any other distractions, and recite and uphold [the mantra] according to the Dharma.
"At that time, there shall be the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha and the Bodhisattva Candraprabha, together with immeasurable rishis, who will come to serve as witnesses and increase its efficacy."
At that time, I shall illuminate and behold [all things] with my thousand eyes and protect and sustain them with my thousand hands.
From this point forward, I shall be able to receive and uphold all the secular scriptures of the world;
furthermore, I shall also master all the magical arts of the heterodox paths and the Vedic treatises.
For those who recite and uphold this divine mantra, the eighty-four thousand types of diseases in the world shall all be cured; there will be none that do not heal.
It can also cause all ghosts and spirits to submit, bring down the various heavenly Māras, and subdue all non-Buddhists.

If, while in the mountains or wilds, one recites sutras or practices seated meditation, and various mountain spirits, miscellaneous demons, *wangliang*, ghosts, and deities should crossingly harass and disturb them such that their minds are not settled, by reciting this mantra once, all these ghosts and deities will be completely bound.

"If one can recite and uphold this according to the Dharma and give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, I shall then command all the benevolent deities, dragon kings, and Vajrapāṇis to constantly follow and protect them, never leaving their side, guarding them as one would one's own eyes or one's own life."
He spoke these verses as an injunction:
"I dispatch the Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada, Ucchuṣma, Kumbhīra, and Aṅkuśin, along with the eight classes of Malla-rākṣasas and Śaṅkara;
they shall always provide protection for those who uphold [this teaching]."
I dispatch Mahānārāyaṇa, Vajraratha, and Kapila;
they shall always protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch Vasurakṣa and Pūrṇabhadra-cāmaracchattra; they shall always protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch Saccaka Māhila and Kūlaṇḍaka Pañcika to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch King Piyakāra and Piṅgala Sāhara to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch Brahmā Triṃśa and the five classes of Śuddhāvāsa and Yāma devas to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch the King of the Śakras and the thirty-three gods, Mahāmati-guṇa and Vajrapāṇi, to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Mother of Spirits, and their hosts of great power,
to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch King Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa, to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch the Golden Peacock King and the assembly of twenty-eight great ṛṣis to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch Maṇibhadra, the Great General Śaṅkha, and Pāñcika to constantly protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch Nanda and Upananda, The nāgas Pāṭala and Elāpattra;
They shall always protect those who uphold [this teaching].
I dispatch asuras, gandharvas, Garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas; They shall always protect those who uphold [this teaching].
"I dispatch the deities of water, fire, lightning, and thunder, as well as the Kumbhāṇḍa King and the Piśācas, to constantly provide protection for those who receive and uphold [this mantra].

These various benevolent deities, along with the divine dragon kings, the divine mothers, and their daughters, each have five hundred retinues; these powerful yakṣas shall always follow and protect those who recite and maintain this Great Compassionate Divine Mantra."
If that person stays in a deserted mountain or a vast wilderness, sleeping alone and solitary, these benevolent deities will take turns guarding them by night, warding off calamities and obstacles.
If one is in a deep mountain and loses the way, by reciting this mantra, benevolent deities and dragon kings will transform themselves into virtuous people and show them the correct path.
If one is in mountain forests or wildernesses where water and fire are scarce, because the Dragon King protects them, he manifests water and fire.
Furthermore, for those who recite and uphold [this name], Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva speaks these verses of cooling relief that eliminate calamities:
"If one travels through wildernesses, mountains, or marshes, And encounters tigers, wolves, and various evil beasts,"
Serpents, vipers, spirits, enchantments, and goblins— upon hearing this incantation recited,
none shall be able to cause harm. Should one travel upon rivers, lakes, or the vast oceans, the venomous dragons,
sea serpents, makaras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, fish, turtles, and tortoises— all shall hide themselves away upon hearing this incantation recited.
If one encounters an army array or is surrounded by bandits, or is robbed of wealth and treasures by evil men,
by sincerely reciting this Great Compassion Mantra, they will give rise to a heart of compassion and return the way they came.
If one’s body is seized by royal officials, Imprisoned in a jail with shackles and fetters,
By sincerely reciting the Dharani of Great Compassion, The officials will spontaneously show favor and release them.
If one enters the homes of those who practice wild ways or sorcery, and their food or drink contains poison intended to harm,
by sincerely reciting this Dharani of Great Compassion, the poisonous drugs will be transformed into ambrosial nectar.
When a woman faces the ordeal of childbirth, Malevolent spirits create obstacles and her suffering is unbearable;
If she sincerely recites the Dharani of Great Compassion, The ghosts and gods will retreat and scatter, allowing for a peaceful birth.
When malevolent dragons and pestilential spirits spread poisonous vapors, And feverish diseases assail one so that life is about to end,
If one invokes and recites the Great Compassion Mantra with a sincere heart, The epidemic will be eliminated and one’s lifespan will be prolonged.
When dragons and ghosts circulate various toxic swellings, And carbuncles, sores, pus, and blood cause unbearable pain,
If one recites the Great Compassion Mantra with a sincere heart, Spitting thrice, the toxic swellings will dissolve as one speaks.
When sentient beings are turbid and evil, giving rise to unwholesome acts, Casting spells of sorcery, uttering curses, and binding themselves in enmity—
If they recite this Dharani of Great Compassion with a sincere heart, The sorcery and curses will return to the person who originated them.
When evil arises and the Dharma is extinguished in the age of turbidity, the fire of lust blazes and the mind becomes deluded;
one abandons one’s wife and husband for external attachments, harboring perverse thoughts day and night without a moment’s pause.
If one can recite this mantra of Great Compassion, the fire of lust will be extinguished and the perverse mind eliminated.
"If I were to extensively praise the power of this mantra, I could extol it for an entire kalpa without reaching its limit.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed Brahmā, saying:
"Recite this mantra five times; take thread of five colors to make a cord, recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, tie twenty-one knots, and fasten it around the neck."
"This dhāraṇī was spoken by ninety-nine billion Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past.
Those Buddhas [taught it] so that practitioners who have not yet fulfilled their cultivation of the six perfections may quickly fulfill them,
and so that those who have not yet resolved for bodhicitta may quickly give rise to that resolve."
If there are śrāvakas who have not yet realized the fruits [of the path], it is so that they may quickly realize them.
If there are any seers and immortals within the trichiliocosm who have not yet resolved upon supreme bodhicitta, it is so that they may quickly resolve their minds upon it.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the faculty of faith in the Mahāyāna, by the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī, may the seeds of the Mahāyāna and the sprouts of the Dharma cause them to grow.
"By the power of my skillful means and compassion, I shall cause all their needs to be fulfilled.
If sentient beings in the three miserable realms, even in the most remote and dark places within a trichiliocosm, hear this mantra of mine, they shall all be freed from suffering."

There are bodhisattvas who have not yet reached the first stage; in order to cause them to attain it swiftly, and even to cause them to attain the ten stages of abiding (*bhūmi*), as well as to cause them to reach the stage of Buddhahood, they naturally achieve the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics.

"If a śrāvaka hears this dhāraṇī even once it passes through their ears, and practices or transcribes this dhāraṇī, abiding in accordance with the Dharma with a straightforward mind, they shall attain the four fruits of the śramaṇa without seeking them."
"If, within this trichiliocosm, I could cause the mountains, rivers, rocky cliffs, and the four great oceans to boil over;
cause Mount Sumeru and the Iron Ring Mountains to tremble;
and further cause them to be shattered like fine dust, while causing all sentient beings therein to resolve upon unsurpassed bodhicitta."

"If there are sentient beings who seek their aspirations in the present life, by maintaining the pure observance of the precepts for twenty-one days and reciting this dhāraṇī, their wishes will surely be fulfilled."
From the limits of birth and death to the limits of birth and death, all evil karma is completely extinguished.
Within this great trichiliocosm, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Brahmās, Śakras, the Four Heavenly Kings, seers, and dragon kings shall all bear witness and know it.

“If there are humans or devas who recite and uphold this dhāraṇī, and if such a person bathes in a river, a stream, or the great ocean, any sentient beings therein who are touched by the water from that person’s body shall have all their evil karma and grave offenses completely extinguished. They will immediately attain rebirth in a pure land in another direction, being born miraculously from a lotus flower, and will no longer receive a womb-born, moisture-born, or egg-born body—how much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it?”

"If one who recites and upholds [this mantra] travels upon a road and a great wind arises, blowing against this person's body, hair, and clothing, and as the wind passes below, if any class of sentient beings receives the wind from that person's drifting body and it blows against them, all their heavy sins and evil karma will be completely extinguished; they shall no longer undergo retribution in the three evil realms and will always be born before the Buddhas."
"You should know that the merit and karmic reward for one who upholds [this] are inconceivable.

For those who recite and maintain this dharani, whatever sounds issue from their mouths—whether good or evil—all Maras, externalists, devas, nagas, ghosts, and spirits who hear them will perceive them as the pure sound of the Dharma; they will all give rise to a heart of reverence toward that person, honoring them as if they were a Buddha."
"One who recites and upholds this dhāraṇī should be known as the treasury of the Buddha-body, for they are cherished by the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of ninety-nine billion Ganges Rivers."
One should know that such a person is a treasury of light, for they are illumined by the radiance of all Tathāgatas.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of compassion, for they constantly rescue sentient beings through dhāraṇīs.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of the sublime Dharma, because they universally encompass all dharani-doors.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of meditative concentration, because hundreds of thousands of samadhis are constantly manifest before them.
One should know that such a person is the treasury of space, for they constantly contemplate sentient beings with the wisdom of emptiness.
One should know that such a person is the treasury of fearlessness, for the nāgas, devas, and benevolent spirits constantly protect and uphold them.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of sublime speech, for the sound of their dhāraṇī from the mouth never ceases.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of permanence, for they cannot be destroyed by the calamities of the evil kalpas.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of liberation, for neither celestial Māras nor non-Buddhist paths can detain them.
One should know that such a person is a treasury of the King of Medicine, for they constantly heal the illnesses of sentient beings through dhāraṇīs.
You should know that such a person is a treasury of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), for they attain mastery while traveling through the buddha-fields.
The merits of such a person cannot be fully extolled.
"Good son!..."
Furthermore, if there is a person who, weary of the sufferings of the world, seeks the bliss of longevity, they should dwell in a secluded and pure place, establish a boundary through purification,
and wear consecrated garments.
Whether it be water, food, incense, or medicine, if one recites the mantra over them one hundred and eight times and then consumes them, one will certainly attain longevity.
If one can establish the boundary according to the ritual and maintain the practice according to the dharma, all things will be accomplished.
As for the method of establishing the boundary (*sīmā-bandha*): take a knife, recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, and draw lines on the ground to form the boundary.
Alternatively, take pure water, recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, and scatter it in the four directions to form the boundary.
Alternatively, take white mustard seeds, recite the mantra over them twenty-one times, and scatter them in the four directions to establish a boundary.
Or, one may establish a boundary wherever the mind reaches through visualization. Or, take pure ashes, recite the mantra over them twenty-one times, and use them to establish a boundary.
Alternatively, one may recite a mantra over five-colored threads twenty-one times and encircle the four sides with them as a boundary;
all shall attain [success].
"If one can receive and maintain this according to the Dharma, the fruit will naturally be realized."
If one merely hears the name of this dhāraṇī, even the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable kalpas will be extinguished; how much more so for those who recite and uphold it?
If one obtains and recites this divine mantra, one should know that such a person has already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and has extensively planted roots of goodness.

"If one can, for the sake of all sentient beings, extract them from their suffering and hardships by reciting and upholding this according to the Dharma, you should know that such a person is one who possesses great compassion."

Not long after attaining Buddhahood, all sentient beings whom he beholds are made to recite [the teachings] so that they may hear them with their own ears, thereby establishing the causes for their enlightenment. The merit of such a person is immeasurable and boundless; it cannot be fully extolled.

"If one can apply oneself with sincere devotion, maintain the fast and precepts, and for the sake of all sentient beings repent for the sins of past karma while also repenting for one's own various evil karmas accumulated over immeasurable kalpas; and if one recites this dhāraṇī from the mouth with constant flow, without a single sound ceasing, then the four fruits of the śramaṇa will be realized in this very life."
For those of sharp faculties and wisdom who contemplate skillful means, even attaining the fruit of the ten stages is not difficult; how much less so the minor worldly blessings and rewards?
There is no aspiration that shall not be fulfilled.

"If one wishes to summon a ghost, take a wild human skull and wash it clean; then establish a ritual altar before an image of the Thousand-Eyed One and offer various incenses, flowers, food, and drink. Doing this daily for seven days, the ghost will surely appear in person and obey whatever commands one gives."
"If one wishes to summon the Four Heavenly Kings, one should burn sandalwood while reciting the mantra.
This is because the power of this Bodhisattva’s vow of great compassion is profound and heavy, and because the majestic spiritual authority of this dhāraṇī is vast and great."
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"If there is a land where calamities arise, and the king of that land governs by means of the True Dharma, treats people with leniency, does not wrong sentient beings, and pardons those who have committed offenses; if he then, for seven days and seven nights, applies himself with physical and mental diligence to recite and uphold this divine mantra of the Great Compassionate Heart Dhāraṇī, all calamities in that land will be entirely extinguished, the five grains will flourish in abundance, and the myriad subjects will enjoy peace and happiness."

"Furthermore, if one is beset by enemies from other lands who repeatedly invade and harass, the common people are unsettled, high ministers plot rebellion, pestilence spreads, floods and droughts are不调 (disorderly), and the sun and moon lose their proper courses."

When such various calamities arise, one should fashion an image of the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes, facing the western direction, and offer worship with utmost sincerity using various incenses, flowers, banners, pennants, jeweled canopies, or food and drink of a hundred flavors.
That king was furthermore able, for seven days and seven nights, to maintain physical and mental diligence in reciting and upholding such wondrous verses of this dhāraṇī.

Consequently, foreign enemies immediately submitted of their own accord; each returned to governing their own territories, no longer causing mutual disturbance or affliction, and the lands became united as they turned toward one another with hearts of loving-kindness.
The princes and the hundred officials all practiced loyalty and sincerity; the consorts, queens, and court ladies showed filial piety and respect toward the king.
The various dragons and spirits protected his kingdom.
"The rains will fall in their proper seasons, fruits and grains will be abundant, and the people will rejoice.

Furthermore, if within a household there occurs a great calamity or illness, if a hundred strange portents arise together, or if ghosts, spirits, and malevolent demons harass and disturb the home; or if wicked people maliciously create strife and slander to plot harm against one another, such that the members of the family, both great and small, internal and external, are in discord—one should establish a ritual altar before the Image of Thousand-Eyed Great Compassion and, with a sincere heart, invoke Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva."
"If one recites this dhāraṇī a full thousand times, all such evil matters as described above will be entirely extinguished, and one shall forever attain peace and security.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the name of this mantra?
How should it be received and upheld?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This divine mantra has various names.
One name is:
Vast and Perfectly Complete."
One name:
Unobstructed Great Compassion.
One name:
The Dharani for Saving from Suffering;
also known as:
The Dharani for Extending Life.
First name:
Dharani for Extinction of Evil Destinies.
Second name: [as above].
The Dhāraṇī for Destroying Obstructions of Evil Karma;
also known as:
The Dhāraṇī that Fulfills All Wishes.
First name:
Dhāraṇī of Sovereignty over the Mind.
Second name:
"The *dhāraṇī* for swiftly transcending the higher stages.
Thus should it be upheld.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the name of this bodhisattva mahāsattva who is so skillfully able to proclaim such a dhāraṇī?”
The Buddha said:
"This bodhisattva is named 'Avalokiteśvara,' also named 'Pāśahasta,' and also named 'Sahasraraśminetra.'"

“Good son! This Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses inconceivable power of majestic virtue. In the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas, he had already attained Buddhahood, being named Tathāgata Saddharmaprabhāsa.”
By the power of his great compassion and vows, he manifests as a bodhisattva in order to inspire all bodhisattvas and to bring peace, happiness, and maturity to all sentient beings.
"You great assembly—bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, Brahmās, Śakras, nāgas, and spirits—all should pay him homage and must not give rise to contempt."
All humans and devas must constantly make offerings [to them].
By single-mindedly reciting their names, one attains immeasurable merit, extinguishes immeasurable transgressions, and at the end of life, is reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“The divine mantra spoken by this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is true and not false.
If you wish to invite this Bodhisattva to come, recite the mantra over *cukkuḷa* incense—*cukkuḷa* incense is *agaru* (aloewood)—twenty-one times and burn it; the Bodhisattva will then arrive.”

"If one is afflicted by a cat-spirit, take the skull of a dead cat named Mṛḍitana and burn it to ash. Mix this with pure clay and mold it into the shape of a cat. Before an image of the Thousand-Eyed One, consecrate an iron blade one hundred and eight times with mantras and cut the figure into pieces, making exactly one hundred and eight segments. Recite the mantra once for each segment and call out the spirit's name once; then the affliction will be permanently cured and no longer recur."

"If one is afflicted by *gūḍa* poison, take the medicinal drug *karpūra* (camphor) and blend it with an equal portion of *candana* (sandalwood), using one *śeṣa* (one *lǐ*) of well-water to boil them together. Take one *śeṣa* of the resulting decoction and, before an image of the Thousand-Eyed One, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times; upon consuming it, one will immediately recover."
"If one is bitten by a venomous snake or scorpion, take powdered dried ginger, recite the mantra over it seventeen times, and apply it to the wound; it will be cured immediately.

If one is maliciously plotted against by an enemy, take clean earth, or flour, or wax, and fashion it into the form of that person. Before an image of the Thousand-Eyed One, recite the mantra over an iron blade one hundred and eight times, cutting off one piece with each recitation while calling out the person's name. When all one hundred and eight pieces have been burned, that person will immediately become joyful, and for the rest of their life, they will be grave and sincere, feeling mutual love and respect."

"If there are those suffering from eye diseases—whether they be those with cataracts, those who are color-blind or have dim vision, or those with white opacities, red films, or lack of light—one should take one fruit each of the three types: *harītakī*, *āmalaka*, and *vibhītaka*. Having taken these, one should pound and grind them finely."
While grinding it, one must strictly maintain purity; do not allow a woman who has recently given birth, nor pigs or dogs, to see it.
Reciting the Buddha’s name within the mouth, mix white honey or human breast milk with it and apply it as an ointment to the eyes.
As for applying human milk, it must be the breast milk of a male child; the milk of a female will not suffice.

Once the medicine has been compounded, one must recite the mantra one thousand and eight times before an image of the Thousand-Eyed One and apply it to the eyes. After seven full days, while staying in a secluded room and avoiding the wind, the eyes will grow back.
Those who suffer from congenital blindness or white opacities will find their vision miraculously restored through its magnificent brilliance.
If one is afflicted by malaria, take the skins of a tiger, leopard, jackal, or wolf, recite the mantra over them twenty-one times, and wear them upon the body; the illness will be immediately cured.
The lion skin is the most superior.
If one is bitten by a snake, take the garment worn by the person who was bitten, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and apply it to the wound; then one will immediately recover.

"If one suffers from a malignant malaria that enters the heart, causing fainting and the desire to die, take one piece of peach resin, about the size of a peach, and boil it with one *sheng* of clear water until reduced to half a *sheng*. Recite the mantra seven times over it and drink it all at once; one will immediately recover."
Do not allow a woman to decoct this medicine.

If one suffers from *chuanshi* (contagious wasting), *guiqi* (demonic vapors), or chronic illnesses caused by *fushi* (buried corpses), take *zhuojuluo* incense, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and burn it to fumigate the nostrils.
Furthermore, take seven pills the size of rabbit droppings, recite the mantra twenty-one times over them, and swallow them; the illness will be cured immediately.
One must be careful regarding alcohol, meat, the five pungent vegetables, and harsh speech.

If one takes *manasīla*—which is realgar—and mixes it with white mustard seeds and salt made from a seal-stamped mold, reciting the mantra twenty-one times, and burns it beneath the bed of the sick child, the spirit causing the illness will immediately be seized by Māra and flee, not daring to remain.
"If one suffers from deafness, one should consecrate sesame oil with mantras and apply it to the ears; it will be cured immediately.

If one suffers from hemiplegia on one side, such that the ears and nose are obstructed and the hands and feet do not respond, one should take sesame oil and boil it with agarwood (śrīkhaṇḍa), consecrate it twenty-one times, and rub it upon the body; one will be permanently healed."
Furthermore, another method is to take pure cow ghee, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and apply it; this will also effect a cure.
If one suffers from difficult labor, take sesame oil, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and rub it into the navel and the vulva of the woman in childbirth; she will then give birth easily.

"If a woman is pregnant and the fetus dies within her womb, take one *liang* of *apāmārga* grass (also known as *gokṣura*), mix it with two *sheng* of clear water, and boil until one *sheng* remains. Recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, then drink it; the fetus will immediately come out without pain."
If the placenta does not emerge, one should also take this medicine, and it will be cured immediately.

If one suddenly suffers from unbearable heart pain, known as "Dunshi-zhu" (the wandering corpse-demon affliction), take one whole nutmeg of *junzhu lu* incense and *xunlu* incense that has formed a nipple-like protrusion; recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, chew it in the mouth and swallow it in whatever quantity is necessary until vomiting occurs, and one will be cured immediately.
Be careful regarding the five pungent vegetables, alcohol, and meat.
"If one is afflicted by a burn from fire, take warm gomaya—the dung of a black ox—and recite the mantra twenty-one times; apply it to the wound, and it will immediately heal."

"If one suffers from heartworms gnawing at the heart, take half a *sheng* of the urine of a white horse from which *gorocanā* has been taken, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and ingest it; one will immediately recover."
In severe cases, one *sheng* [of liquid] will emerge with worms as white as silk cords.

"If one suffers from *dingchuang* (boils), take the leaves of the *ling-suo* plant and pound them to extract the juice. Recite the mantra twenty-one times and drip it onto the sores; the roots will be pulled out immediately, and the patient will recover at once."

"If one suffers from flies stinging the eyes, take the juice of *kharoṭaka*—fresh donkey dung—filter it, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, and apply it to the eyes before going to bed at night; the affliction will be immediately cured."

"If one suffers from abdominal pain, mix [the medicine] with well-water and thirty-seven grains of stamped salt; recite the mantra thirty-seven times and drink half a sheng, and the illness will be cured immediately."

"If one suffers from red eyes, or has protruding flesh in the eyes, or has cataracts, take the leaves of *śaśāmi* (the jujube tree), pound them, and strain to obtain the juice. Recite the mantra twenty-one times over it, soak a copper coin in it overnight, then recite the mantra seven more times. Place it in the eye, and it will be cured immediately."

"If one suffers from fear of the night, feels uneasy and terrified, or is startled and afraid when entering or leaving, take white thread to make a cord, recite the mantra over it twenty-one times, tie twenty-one knots, and fasten it around the neck; the terror will then be dispelled."
Not only does it remove fear, but it also extinguishes transgressions.

"If calamities should arise unexpectedly within one's household, take branches of the pomegranate tree and cut them into one thousand and eight pieces, each an inch long. Anoint both ends with ghee, curd, and honey; for every incantation, burn one piece, until all one thousand and eight have been exhausted. All calamities will be entirely eliminated; this must be performed before the Buddha."
"If one takes white calamus, recites the mantra over it twenty-one times, and ties it upon the right arm, one will prevail over others in all places of combat or in debates on doctrine."

"If one takes the leaves and branches of the śaśami tree, cuts them into inch-long segments, and anoints both ends with pure cow ghee and white honey, reciting the mantra once for each segment while burning them—one thousand and eight segments in total—three times daily, with one thousand and eight recitations per session, for seven full days, the mantra master will personally awaken to penetrating wisdom."

"If one wishes to subjugate powerful spirits and deities, one should take *ariṣṭaka* wood (the *muhuanzi* tree), recite the mantra over it seven times seven times, and burn it in fire; furthermore, it must be smeared with ghee, curd, and honey, and the rite must be performed before an image of the One of Great Compassion."

If one takes one *liang* of *hulu-chan* (cow bezoar), places it in a crystal bottle, and sets it before an image of Mahākaruṇika, reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times; then, by anointing the body and marking the forehead with it, all devas, nāgas, ghosts, spirits, humans, and non-humans will be filled with joy.

"If there is anyone whose body is bound by shackles and chains, take the droppings of a white dove, recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times, smear them upon the hands, and rub them against the shackles and chains; the shackles and chains will fall away of their own accord."

"If there are husband and wife who are discordant, their relationship like water and fire, one should take the tail feathers of a mandarin duck and recite the mantra over them one thousand and eight times before an image of Avalokiteśvara of Great Compassion. If they wear these, they will henceforth for the rest of their lives remain joyful and mutually affectionate and respectful."

"If there are field seedlings or the five types of fruit that have been eaten by insects, take pure ash, pure sand, or pure water, recite the mantra over them twenty-one times, and scatter them around the four sides of the field seedlings; the insects will immediately retreat and disperse."
"If one sprinkles water consecrated with mantras upon fruit trees, the insects on the trees will not dare to eat the fruit.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If you wish for wealth and abundance, with various kinds of precious jewels and requisites, you should [worship] the Hand of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel."
If one seeks peace and security from various forms of unrest, one should focus on the hand holding the noose.
If one seeks relief from diseases within the abdomen, one should focus on the hand holding the precious bowl.
If one wishes to subdue all *piśāca* spirits and ghosts, one should focus on the sword hand.
If one wishes to subdue all celestial māras and demons, one should focus on the *vajra* hand.
If one wishes to subdue all enemies, one should focus on the hand holding the vajra.
If one is fearful or uneasy in any situation, one should focus on the hand granting fearlessness.
If one has blurred vision and lacks clarity, one should focus on the Sun-Essence Maṇi hand.
If one seeks coolness for the sake of curing diseases caused by heat and toxins, one should focus on the Moon-Essence Maṇi hand.
If one desires honor in office and advancement in rank, one should pray to the deity holding the precious bow.
If one desires to meet with virtuous friends early on, one should pray to the deity holding the precious arrow.
If one seeks to cure various ailments of the body, one should look to the hand holding the willow branch.
If one seeks to eliminate evil obstacles and hardships of the body, one should look to the hand holding the white fly-whisk.
If one wishes to become a benefactor who brings harmony to all kinsmen and retinues, one should focus on the hand holding the ewer.
If one wishes to expel all tigers, wolves, jackals, leopards, and other malevolent beasts, one should focus on the hand holding the shield.
If one wishes to be well-situated at all times and places and to avoid the perils of official service, one should [worship] the one with the axe and halberd in hand.
If one wishes for male and female servants and attendants, one should [worship] the one with the jade ring in hand.
If one seeks various meritorious virtues, one should attend to the White Lotus-Handed One.
If one desires to attain rebirth in the pure lands of the ten directions, one should attend to the Blue Lotus-Handed One.
If one wishes to become a possessor of great wisdom, one should attend to the Jewel Mirror Hand.
If one wishes to behold all Buddhas of the ten directions face-to-face, one should attend to the Purple Lotus Hand.
If for one who seeks treasures hidden in the earth, [one should worship] the deity with the jewel casket in hand.
If for one who seeks the path of the immortals, [one should worship] the deity with the five-colored clouds in hand.
If for one who seeks rebirth in the Brahma Heaven, [one should worship] the deity with the *muñjakeśa* grass in hand.
If one wishes to be reborn in the palaces of the various devas, one should attend to the deity with the red lotus in hand.
If one wishes to repel rebellious enemies from other regions, one should attend to the deity with the jeweled spear in hand.
If one wishes to summon all the devas and benevolent spirits, one should look to the hand holding the precious conch.
If one wishes to command all the ghosts and spirits, one should look to the hand holding the skull-topped staff.
If one wishes for the Buddhas of the ten directions to swiftly extend their hands to grant them aid, one should focus on the hand holding the rosary.
If one wishes to achieve all sublime and wondrous Brahma-sounds, one should focus on the hand holding the jeweled bell.
If one desires eloquence and skillful speech as a karmic result of oral activity, one should worship the deity with the jewel-seal hand.
If one desires to be constantly protected by benevolent deities and nāga kings, one should worship the deity with the iron hook hand from Kuśinagara.
If one wishes to compassionately protect and shelter all sentient beings, one should look at the hand holding the mendicant’s staff (*khakkhara*).
If one wishes for all sentient beings to always respect, love, and cherish one another, one should look at the hands joined in *añjali* (palms-pressed gesture).
If you wish that in every birth you shall not be separated from the presence of the Buddhas, you should [focus] on the hand of the transformation Buddha.
If you wish that in life after life you shall always dwell within the palaces of the Buddhas and never receive a body born from a womb, you should [focus] on the hand of the transformation palace.
If for one who is widely learned and a great scholar, it should be the hand holding the precious scripture.
If for one whose bodhicitta never regresses from this present body until the attainment of Buddhahood, it should be the hand holding the non-regressing golden wheel.

If one wishes for the Buddhas of the ten directions to swiftly come and bestow the empowerment of anointing upon the crown of the head, one should visualize the hands of the emanated Buddha upon the crown.
If one wishes for fruits, melons, and various grains and crops, one should visualize the grape-hand.
"Such dharmas as may be sought number in the thousands; what I have now spoken is but a brief summary.
Then the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha, for the sake of those who receive and uphold the Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī, spoke this great divine mantra to protect them:

*Namo buddhānām* (1) *Namo dharmāya mahate* (2) *Namaḥ saṃghāya tāyanaye* (3) *Tiribuvisasaṃbuddhadhyāna-mahā* "If one recites this mantra, all sins shall be extinguished; it can also ward off demons and eliminate celestial calamities."

"If one recites this mantra once and performs one prostration to the Buddha, doing so three times each day—reciting the mantra and prostrating to the Buddha—one shall, in future lives, obtain a body with every single feature perfectly handsome and pleasing as a karmic reward."
The Bodhisattva Candraprabha likewise spoke this dhāraṇī mantra for the sake of practitioners to protect them:

"Śindhite susuta 1 | Ajñamite uduta 2 | Śaṅkita 3 | Parādite 4 | Yamijrute uduta 5 | Krodhite ḍhakimaṭe 6 | Svāhā. Recite this mantra five times, take thread of five colors, fashion it into a protective cord, and tie it upon the afflicted area.
"This mantra was spoken by as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in forty Ganges Rivers; I now speak it as well.

It is for the sake of providing protection for all practitioners, for the removal of all obstacles and difficulties, for the elimination of all evil diseases and pains, for the accomplishment of all wholesome dharmas, and for remaining far removed from all fears."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"With a deeply pure mind, you should receive and uphold this dhāraṇī, and propagate it widely throughout Jambudvīpa so that it shall not be interrupted."

"This dhāraṇī can bring great benefit to sentient beings throughout the three realms; for those whose bodies are afflicted by any illness or suffering, if they treat it with this dhāraṇī, there shall be none who do not recover."
"This great divine mantra can cause even withered trees to sprout branches, twigs, flowers, and fruit; how much more so for sentient beings who possess consciousness?"
If one has a physical ailment that does not improve through treatment, such a thing is impossible.
"Good son! The majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī is inconceivable!"
Inconceivable! One's praise could never be exhausted.
If one has not extensively planted roots of goodness since the distant past, even their name cannot be heard, let alone be seen.
"You great assembly—gods, humans, nāgas, and spirits—having heard my praise, you should all rejoice.
Should anyone slander this dhāraṇī, they would be slandering those ninety-nine billion Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."

If one conceives doubt and lacks faith in this dhāraṇī, you should know that such a person will forever lose the great benefit; for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, they shall constantly sink into the evil realms with no time of escape, never seeing the Buddha, never hearing the Dharma, and never beholding the Saṅgha.

When all those in the assembly—the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, Vajrapāṇi, Brahmā, Śakra, the four heavenly kings, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits—heard the Buddha Tathāgata praise this dhāraṇī, they were all filled with joy and respectfully practiced according to his instructions.
The Sūtra of the Great, Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Heart of Great Compassion Dharani of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes.
